title: Boundary Free Energies, Quenched Mixing, and Gibbs-State Selection in Disordered Ising Models
authors: Mauris Chueng, Hexiang Wang, Keheng Zhu
abstract: We study boundary free energies and half-space responses in nearest-neighbor disordered Ising models. First, we prove the existence of fixed-depth tangential pressure and identify its derivative almost everywhere with the limiting boundary response. Second, under quenched exponential boundary-response mixing, we prove Gibbs-state selection independence and exponential convergence of finite-depth pressures. We further show that uniform one-spin mixing yields DLR uniqueness and Gaussian normal localization, and verify the required mixing conditions whenever $(2d-1)\mathbb E\tanh(β\vert{}J\vert{})<1$. Finally, we establish an all-face surface limit in the bounded Dobrushin regime and provide counterexamples that delimit general surface and stiffness claims.
summary: This work provides a rigorous mathematical analysis of disordered Ising models, focusing on how boundary conditions and disorder affect the system's free energy. The authors establish key convergence theorems for boundary free energies and prove conditions under which the system's thermodynamic state is uniquely determined (Gibbs-state selection). It advances the mathematical understanding of disordered critical phenomena.
main_problem: The paper investigates the mathematical properties of boundary free energies, quenched mixing, and the selection of the correct Gibbs state in disordered Ising models.
main_result: Key results include proving the existence of fixed-depth tangential pressure and establishing Gibbs-state selection independence under specific mixing conditions.
method: The analysis employs advanced techniques from statistical mechanics, including concentration inequalities, derivative representations derived from concavity, and stochastic localization arguments.
model_or_system: The study focuses on nearest-neighbor disordered Ising models, characterized by random couplings ($J$) and analyzed on finite volumes that are extrapolated to infinite limits (e.g., half-spaces or infinite strips).
key_observables: Boundary free energies ($\Delta F$), tangential pressure ($p_L(r)$), boundary-response mixing (BRM), and seam-flip differences ($D_n$).
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), dimension ($d \ge 2$), and the mixing condition $(2d-1)\mathbb E	anh( eta|J|) < 1$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on assumptions regarding the geometry (regularity), the existence of certain mixing conditions (e.g., quenched exponential boundary-response mixing), and the ability to control fluctuations via concentration bounds.

paper_structure: The paper develops results by analyzing finite-volume identities, establishing the existence and properties of the tangential pressure limit, proving convergence results under mixing conditions, and concluding with discussions on necessary localization bounds and open problems.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous mathematical techniques used—especially those involving localization, convergence of random fields, and controlling fluctuations in disordered systems—are highly relevant to understanding quantum phase transitions and quantum disordered systems.
